slides.headline: Miami Beach backs car-free Ocean Drive
slides.body: Commissioners voted 7-0 in September 2026 to seek a car closure on Ocean Drive from 5th to 15th streets, Thanksgiving through March 31.

photo.query: Ocean Drive Miami Beach Lummus Park daytime
photo.prompt: Daytime photo looking down Ocean Drive beside Lummus Park, with Art Deco hotels, sidewalk cafes, palm trees, and the 10-block stretch visible

slides.headline: That covers 10 blocks by Lummus Park
slides.body: The stretch runs along the Lummus Park side, across from hotels and sidewalk cafes between 5th and 15th streets.

photo.query: Lummus Park Ocean Drive Miami Beach hotels cafes
photo.prompt: Wide street-level photo of Lummus Park next to Ocean Drive, with hotels, sidewalk cafes, palms, and pedestrians in South Beach

slides.headline: That extends the plan past Valentine’s Day
slides.body: The original proposal reopened the street after Valentine’s Day, and commissioners extended it through March to cover spring break.

photo.query: Ocean Drive Miami Beach pedestrians night
photo.prompt: Night scene on Ocean Drive in South Beach with people walking under neon Art Deco hotel lights and palm trees

slides.headline: Which follows years of opening and closing
slides.body: Ocean Drive closed to cars in 2020 for outdoor dining and distancing, then reopened to cars on Jan. 24, 2022 after nearly two years.

photo.query: Ocean Drive Miami Beach outdoor dining street closure
photo.prompt: Photo of Ocean Drive set up for outdoor dining, with tables in the street, pedestrians, Art Deco buildings, and no car traffic

slides.headline: And cars came back two-way in 2025
slides.body: In February 2025, Miami Beach reopened Ocean Drive to two-way traffic and removed the bike lanes.

photo.query: Ocean Drive Miami Beach traffic cars Art Deco
photo.prompt: Street-level photo of cars moving along Ocean Drive in Miami Beach with Art Deco hotels, palm trees, and busy sidewalks

slides.headline: So the county and FDOT decide next
slides.body: Miami-Dade County and FDOT still have to review and permit the closure, while businesses remain divided over foot traffic, hotel access and congestion on parallel streets.
